bio_en: Tigran Teroyan, known as Vazgen, was a young man of Van who left school to apprentice with an Armenian Protestant tailor and first made his name by fighting off soldiers who were abusing a fellow Armenian. The death of his beloved teacher Agrippasian with Goloshian at Chukh-gyaduk set him on the revolutionary path, and he wrote verse and frequent letters and articles for Droshak. After Peto's departure and death he became the driving force of revolutionary work in Van. After the Van events of 1896 he left the city with the band leader Mikeo of Shatakh and Arshak of Van, and all three fell fighting some 200 soldiers and gendarmes on the plain of Kurubash on 2 January; they were buried at the church of Arark.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. Death year: the text gives 2 January following the 1896 Van events, i.e. probably January 1897; stored year is 1896 - verify.
